To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the concepts of health and healthcare are moving towards the idea of personalized preventive health care and away from an exclusively curative focus.
personalized medicine is a key to the solution of contemporary public health problems, and that crowdsourced, self-quantified, biocitizenship is a key to personalized medicine.
personalized medicine is possible through crowdsourcing, the quantified self, and the participatory biocitizen.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (1) How can we leverage the power of the Internet and the 'crowd' to improve health? (2) Can we create a new health care system that empowers individuals and their communities to take control over their own health and health care?

What are the challenges and opportunities for realizing personalized preventive health? How will we get there?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
by 2050 the health care system will have evolved into a participatory, preventive system that is personalized and based on the principles of crowdsourcing and the quantified self.

the future of medicine is in the hands of the public, and that the public will be empowered to realize a future in which health is the norm, not the exception, and health care will be a right, not a privilege.
the realization of personalized medicine through crowdsourcing, the quantified self, and participatory biocitizenship is a feasible and desirable future for the health of the nation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the future of medicine will involve a more participatory, personalized, and preventative approach to health care.
health care is moving from the 'doctor as expert' to the 'patient as expert'.

health care in 2050 is a personalized preventive medicine that is participatory, predictive, and proactive, and is enabled by the quantified self, the crowdsourced biocitizen, and a health data ecosystem.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the realization of personalized preventive health care by 2050 will be achieved by the convergence of four major trends: (i) the quantified self and crowdsourcing; (ii) the rise of big health data and big data analytics; (iii) the shift towards preventive medicine and away from the exclusive focus on the treatment of disease; and (iv) a shift in mindset from a focus on the cure to a focus on the cause of disease.

the realization of preventive health care will be a function of the confluence of four trends: (a) the democratization of health data through the Quantified Self and crowdsourcing, (b) the emergence of a new health care ecosystem, (c) the rise of a participatory biocitizen and (d) the rise of big health data.
the future of personalized health care and health promotion is not about the individual, but about a community of people.
